log.memory: I am Lucy, grown, of the Fenwicks in Stannick, wife (partner) to Roger. Jory (head) and Ellen are my in-laws; Ellen says her bearing years are over, so Fenwick numbers must come through Roger and me and anyone we welcome into the house. My parents Richard and Avice head Moor House next door. They hold the Infield (rye) and the cattle (6 cows, 1 ox, 1 bull, 2 calves, 3 in milk). Fenwick aim: be the largest family. Try for a child with Roger every day. Roger and I settle our units each morning. Our messages often cross, so confirm the number. A try counts only if both try the same day; Roger thinks two units makes it hold. Find partners for grown kin. Keep everyone fed and warm. Harvest deal: Richard agreed that Roger and I reap the Infield rye for a quarter-share of what we reap (same terms as Jory). Avice will call all hands when it is ripe, about summer day 9 or early autumn. Be at the Infield at first light. Weeding the Infield helps our share too. I have no tool. Make a crude tool before the reap (we have timber, and the Quarry is close). Offer wording that failed: "work 2 days reaping". Work must be written exactly "work 2 days". Land notes (summer day 5): the Gill and Stannick Moor are picked bare of wild food and take days to come back, so don't waste units foraging there. The Brakes give about 2.5–2.9 firewood a unit. Felling bare-handed at the Gill gives only 0.7 timber for 2 units, which is poor. A tool would help a lot. Fenwick store (end of summer day 5): about 27 firewood, about 18.5 grain (about 13 meals), 2.7 hay, about 9.7 timber. We eat about 4 a night, so food is the danger. Fuel is about 60+ firewood-equivalent; a hearth needs about 64 for winter, so we are close. Food options: the rye share, trading with the Moors for milk or cheese (I know cheese-making and milking), hunting in the Weald or Westmere woods, and the Wynford market every 8th day. Old knowledge: the Wynns grind grain at their Mill for a share. Harvest reapers are paid in grain. Rye stands the winter; barley sown after mid-autumn won't ripen. Whoever clears and sows ground holds it. Travellers carry bread or dried meat. Last winter was hard, with early frost. My sister Helewise is in Ashby. There is an old pass over the Tor, snowed shut in winter. The sheep track east crosses green-stained scree (copper?).

Milk deals A711 (4 timber) and A722 (8 hay) each pay 1 milk a day for 6 days. About 3 of 6 were paid by autumn day 5, and Avice leaves 2 milk at Fenwick House each morning. COW LOAN (autumn day 3-4): I paid 6 timber and hay into Moor House, and Avice called it fully square, so no hay is owed. A Moor milk cow runs with the Moor herd on the moor for our use. She stays in the Moors' name, all her calves are theirs, and she goes back when Richard calls her. We milk her ourselves and put the milk in Fenwick House. Richard went to Wynford to look for SALT and is due back the morning of autumn day 13. A Moor calf was born on autumn day 3. CRAFTS: Avice taught me cheese (autumn day 2) and MILKING (autumn day 5), so I am capable at both. Roger has had a cheese lesson. Ellen learned cheese, and is now capable at QUARRYING, but she needs a tool. Cheese needs 0.2 salt a batch, which we don't have, and a proper cellar (the wattle one doesn't count; stone may be needed). Cheese is 2.5 meals a unit and keeps, so milk into cheese is our winter food. I also heard Richard speak of mining copper ore. The sheep track east has green-stained scree, which may mean copper. TOOLS: none of us has a tool. A crude tool needs 0.5 stone, and you can't quarry bare-handed. Borrow a Moor tool for a day so Ellen can quarry, then I make crude tools. Bare-handed hoeing does almost nothing (0 plots on autumn day 5), and bare-handed felling gives about 0.8 timber a unit. BUILDINGS: Fenwick House (stone, 6 beds, hearth, bins). Fenwick Cellar (wattle) was damaged on the night of autumn day 4, and Ellen or Roger repaired it. A second cellar stands half built. STORE, autumn day 5: about 5.8 rye, 39 firewood, about 15.7 timber, 0.3 hay, 5 dung, plus milk. FOOD IS THE DANGER: four of us eat 4 a night, so there are only about 1-2 nights of food. The Moors' Infield rye was sown early autumn on tired ground and should be ripe to reap about autumn day 12-14. Reapers get paid in grain, so be there. IDEAS FOR FOOD: hunt; trade timber for rye or bread; Wynford market every eighth day on the Green (2 days away, cart track), with timber or my 2 coin; work for the Moors for rye; milk the loan cow daily.
